reason: A compound shape adjective ('6–10 pairs of triangular-lobulate [segments]'): triangular with small lobes. The counted part is the leaf segment that follows. It is a quality fragment, not a structure.
A spelling variant of triangular-lobulate: a shape adjective that qualifies the counted segments, not a part name.
Narrower: a tuft domatium is the hair-tuft kind of domatium, found in vein axils. The tuft could also be expressed as a quality of the domatium (bearded/hairy), so no subclass is needed.

target: shoot axis node (PO_0005004) as the position in pattern 14 (count at a position); the bearer is the counted part (flower PO_0009046, branch)
reason: A position phrase: 'flowers 1 or 3 at the nodes', 'branches 2-3 at the nodes'. The count belongs to the flowers or branches, located at the node. Use stem node (PO_0020141) when the axis is the stem.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part_of limbidium (FLOPO_0986075), pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole)
reason: In moss leaf descriptions ('cells of the border large', 'linear cells') the border is the limbidium, which FLOPO already has. Do not map it to root-cap border cells.

'The crest on each side of 3 lobes': the crest's owner is unknown (keel crest of Polygala, seed crest, anther crest), and the Spanish fragment 'ovados' does not help. It is a generic part that needs its organ.

label: dorsal suture
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009030 (carpel)
definition: A cardinal organ part that is the longitudinal line on the abaxial side of a carpel, over its median vein, along which the ovary wall or the fruit derived from it may open.
reason: A standard term for legumes, follicles and capsules that PO lacks. It is not the fruit dehiscence zone (PO_0004707), because the dorsal suture also exists in fruits that do not open along it. It should be proposed to PO together with its sibling 'ventral suture' (the fused carpel margins). The truncated 'hyaline partia...' example may be a misreading.
An OCR misreading of 'μm' ('about 8 fj, wide', '31-36.5 fj, long'). It is a unit, not a structure. It should be fixed in the text normalisation.

target: plant ovary locule (PO_0025266) for ovules, fruit locule (PO_0025270) for seeds, as the position in pattern 14; the bearer is ovule or seed
reason: In older floras 'cell' here means locule ('ovules 6-8 in each cell', 'seeds 2 in each cell'). It is a count at a position, not a plant cell.

Plant cell plus the quality 'large', with no organ ('about 4 large cells', 'cortical layer of 10-12 large cells'). Like 'scale' and 'segment' in the previous review, it is a generic part that needs its organ.

target: spike inflorescence (PO_0030117) + lower (FLOPO_0991377), pattern 18 (position of the bearer in a series)
reason: Which spike in a series (Carex and similar: 'las inferiores remotas'). The 'lower' rule already exists, but its bearer list has 'spikelet' and not 'spike'. Adding 'spike' to it covers this.

target: apex region of perigynium beak (FLOPO_0986070), i.e. the mouth of the beak of the perigynium (PO_0009044)
reason: In Carex the orifice is the opening at the tip of the perigynium beak. 'Entire or emarginate' and 'oblique' describe the apex of the beak.

target: leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517) or leaflet (PO_0020049) + terminal (PATO_0002476), pattern 18
reason: The terminal segment of a divided leaf ('terminal division 3~5-cleft, double-serrate'). 'Division' is a lobe in a pinnatifid leaf and a leaflet or pinna in a compound one. The existing 'terminal' rule covers lobe, segment, pinna and leaflet; choose the class from the leaf type.
A ratio fragment ('espacées de 1-2 fois leur longueur'). It belongs to pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with the internode or spikelet as bearer.

target: petal base (PO_0025146) part_of wing petal (PO_0025325), pattern 12
reason: The claw is the narrowed stalk-like base of the wing petal (PO_0025325 exact). The previous review rejected 'claw' alone only because it lacked an organ; here the organ is given. A shared 'petal claw' class (is_a PO_0025146) is worth considering if claws keep appearing, but the base region is enough for length statements now.

Exact: an old spelling of raphe ('rhaphe 0.8 cm. long'); use seed raphe (PO_0006331) when the seed is the context. The 'muni de raphides' example is a mismatch: raphides are crystals and must not ground here.

'Rhizome composed of up to about t[en] units' and units 'claviformes a subglobosas': these are sympodial segments or tuberous swellings that change from family to family. PO has rhizome (PO_0004542) and rhizome internode (PO_0025204), but neither fits safely.
Exact: the secondary (lateral) veins of the lamina.
Cells of the seed surface ('25–50 μm wide', 'cells smooth'). These are cells of the seed coat's outer epidermis.

label: anthophore
definition: A shoot axis that is an elongated internode of the floral axis between the calyx and the corolla, raising the corolla, androecium and gynoecium above the calyx.
reason: A real floral structure (Caryophyllaceae such as Silene, Capparaceae, Passifloraceae) with no class. It is different from gynophore (PO_0006330), androphore (FLOPO_0986019) and androgynophore (FLOPO_0986018), which lie above the corolla. It should be proposed to PO next to gynophore.

target: flower (PO_0009046) counted in cyme inflorescence (PO_0030126), pattern 3 (count of parts)
reason: '(1–)3-flowered', 'cymes de 1-3 fleurs': a count of the flowers of a cyme, not a separate structure.
A generic outgrowth without its organ ('raised on protuberances ± 1 mm high'). It could be emergence (FLOPO_0986107), tubercle or wart depending on context.
Exact in Rosaceae usage: the cup-shaped receptacle is the hypanthium (floral cup, already a PO synonym).
Exact in context: 'midrib and main laterals', '16–25 main laterals' are the secondary veins coming off the midrib.
A frequency adverb ('pairs of often anisophyllous...'). It belongs to the frequency of an alternative (pattern 8), not to a part.
Narrower: a short cup-shaped staminal tube formed by the connate filament bases (e.g. Amaranthaceae). 'Undulate margin' and 'equal to the sepals' are qualities and relations of that tube.
A ratio fragment ('terminal one up to twice as long as the laterals'). It belongs to pattern 10, with the terminal leaflet or lobe as bearer and the lateral ones as the second term.
Exact: the word was extracted twice ('Palea indurate'). Use the grass palea class, not inflorescence bract (PO_0009054), which the lexicon also lists under 'palea' for Asteraceae receptacle scales.
A density phrase ('commissural veins 8-15 per cm', 'environ 7 par cm'). The bearer is the veins and the value is a count per length, so this is not a part name.
A generic 'lobe' with a developmental state ('only 1-3 lobes developing'), without the organ it belongs to.
